### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s).

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **21** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `707ce6991b147a7ab380f7673b59dc7b69225059` — the merge of head `18b8af0ceaa875796714e2cdb1f5f5d547561566` into base `385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 707ce6991b147a7ab380f7673b59dc7b69225059 && git checkout 707ce6991b147a7ab380f7673b59dc7b69225059
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca 18b8af0ceaa875796714e2cdb1f5f5d547561566 && git checkout -B drift-repro 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca && git merge --no-ff 18b8af0ceaa875796714e2cdb1f5f5d547561566

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 385ea1cce5e1761b36d7e9fbc8b599f5adb07fca` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc13f5644e30ad1adca9350c68d221a53a27f19f`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts + .changeset/sso-body-origins-trust-discovery-only.md, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx

Read at 2026-11-15T19:19Z. First review of this head; claim: comment 6899725201; lane request 6899700369 on mailbox #33873. Independence: implemented and dispatched by security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla.

Read, never reviewed (outside the diff): `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-plugin.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-provider-lifecycle.test.ts`, `packages/platform-objects/src/identity/sys-sso-provider.object.ts`, and the published sources of `better-auth` and `@better-auth/sso` at the locked 1.7.12 (the request context, the hook pipeline, the origin check, the register and update-provider endpoints). Nothing was built or run; every statement below is a reading of the tree.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule: an origin a register or update body names is trusted only for the server-side discovery fetch and validation of that provider, and never as an accepted `Origin` for the request's own origin check, which reads the deployment's configured trusted origins alone.

**The request-origin half holds on every door I could find.**

- The auth instance's `trustedOrigins` option is now the configured list in every arm (configured list; key omitted in production with nothing configured; the localhost trio outside production). No per-request function remains, so no door's origin check, callback or redirect validation can read anything a request carries. On `main` the function added origins for the register and update-provider paths only, so sign-in, callbacks, sign-out, the OIDC authorize gate and every other endpoint read the same list before and after: no legitimate configured flow there moves. Wildcard patterns, the deployment's own origin and env-supplied origins travel the same array path as on a deployment without the SSO relying party, which `main` already exercises.
- The two bridge doors (`/admin/sso/register`, `/admin/sso/update-provider` and its siblings) re-dispatch a request through the vendor handler, so they meet the same static list and the same before-hook; the register allowance reaches them through the hook, which reads the parsed body, not the URL.
- The allowance is scoped to one provider and one request: `ssoDiscoveryCompanionContext` copies the list it is handed, and the vendor merges the hook's answer into a fresh per-dispatch context after its router-level check has run. The shared context is not mutated; I found no cached or shared list and no path for one request's allowance to reach another.
- Vendor discovery on `/sso/register` still receives the body-named origins (issuer and each explicit `oidcConfig` endpoint), and an endpoint that only the discovery document names is still refused.

**The discovery half does not hold on every reader. M1.**

M1 (must-fix) — The before-hook has a second server-side discovery reader for the same provider on the same request: the sign-out-of-IdP capability check (`assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported`, `auth-manager.ts`, calling `judgeSignOutOfIdpCapability`), which runs on `/sso/register` and on `/sso/update-provider` and validates the provider's logout endpoint with the hook-time context's `isTrustedOrigin`. On `main` that context held the body-named origins on both doors. At this head it holds the configured list only: on register the hand-off is the hook's return value, built after this check has already run, and on update there is no hand-off at all. So a register, or an update, from a configured origin that names the provider's issuer or endpoints and saves the switch on is refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp` where `main` saved it, unless the operator lists the identity provider's origin. That is the provider's own discovery validation, the one use the rule says a body-named origin keeps. It is also a second narrowing that nothing declares, and three statements in the change are false for it: the PR body's "the body-named origins ... changed none of its verdicts" for update, the same sentence in the `sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts` header ("An update needs none of them"), and the changeset's "Unchanged: a registration from a configured origin still discovers and registers ...; an update from a configured origin". No test drives a register or update that carries the switch with a body-named origin, so CI is green over it. Either keep the rule on this reader (the body-named origins reach the capability check on both doors, for that check only, with a test pinning each door and a CONTROL that an endpoint the body does not name is still refused), or declare the narrowing in the changeset and PR body with its own remedy and pin it. The Console's Edit Sign-In Options action sends no issuer or endpoint, so it reads the configured list on `main` and here alike; the reach is the vendor doors called with a body that names both.

**Tests.** The new describe pins the request-origin half with the controls asked for: a body-named origin refused as `Origin` on register (issuer and endpoint) and on update (endpoint and issuer) with the rows unchanged; a different-host refusal; a configured origin accepted on register and update; a body-named origin accepted for the vendor's discovery; a discovery-only endpoint still refused; another POST judged on the configured list. `auth-manager.test.ts` pins the three configuration arms as a list, never a function. The gap is M1's reader.

S1 (should-fix) — `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` says an origin "a registration or an update names" is trusted for that provider's discovery and validation. At this head an update's named origin is handed to nothing. Once M1 is settled, make the sentence say what each door does.

N1 (nit) — the changeset subject reads `fix(auth)!` and the PR title `fix(plugin-auth)!`.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset. That is the level AGENTS.md sets for a breaking change that moves no metadata protocol. The changeset carries the BREAKING banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`, and nothing stored changes shape, so the disposition fits), the from and to of the option (per-request function to the configured list), who moves, and the one-line remedy (send from a configured origin, or add the page's origin to `trustedOrigins` / `OS_CORS_ORIGIN`). For the narrowing it names, the declaration is complete. It is incomplete for M1's second narrowing, and its Unchanged list overstates.

CI at this head: 62 check-runs, all completed; 40 success, 21 skipped, 1 cancelled. The cancelled run is a `Check Changeset` run superseded by a later `Check Changeset` success on the same head. Nothing is running or red. Green CI does not cover M1: no test reaches it.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The hand-off rides a vendor seam (a before-hook's context answer merged per dispatch, arrays replaced) that the companion origins already use; a vendor upgrade that changes that merge moves both, and the new CONTROL for a foreign endpoint would go red, which is the right alarm.
- The before-hook host gains `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` and the auth-instance host drops `isSsoWired`; both host interfaces and the wiring in `auth-manager.ts` agree.
- Security discipline: this record stays at the rule layer. One pre-existing observation about the discovery allowance, unchanged by this head and outside the rule this PR claims, is held by the review seat outside this record and is not graded here.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the published surface on `main`: the declared narrowing makes the spec's own refusal real. `trustedOrigins` is documented as the deployment's list, and a request body adding to the list its own origin check reads was never a declared capability, so taking it away removes nothing a consumer was promised; the only client that moves is the one the changeset names. Moving the body-named origins onto the per-endpoint seam, next to the companion origins, is the right shape: one seam, one request, one provider.

The design is not finished, though. The rule names "discovery fetch and validation of that provider", and the tree has two readers of that kind on these doors: the vendor's, which the hand-off reaches, and the plugin's own capability check in the same hook, which it does not. The change reasons about the vendor's reader alone, on both doors, and that is where M1 comes from. A must-fix found here is a FAIL.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `f87435b23aa0967d68d93ecb38f1b9170a5c23e9`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-auth-instance.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager-before-hook.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/auth-manager.test.ts + .changeset/sso-body-origins-trust-discovery-only.md, content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx

Read at 2026-11-15T20:11Z. Delta review of this head against FAIL 6899874194 at dc13f564; claim: comment 6900490763; taken on patrol as owed. Independence: implemented and dispatched by security#1 (sunhaolin); reviewed by os-tesla.

Read, never reviewed (outside the diff): `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/sso-sign-out-of-idp.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/register-sso-provider.ts`, and the published sources of `better-auth` and `@better-auth/sso` at the locked 1.7.12 (the request context's origin predicate and its pattern match, the hook pipeline). Nothing was built or run; every statement below is a reading of the tree at this head, of the three commits since `dc13f564` (`a9ed9977` pins, `fb2572c8` fix, `f87435b2` docs and changeset text), and of the full diff against the merge base `d3bea96d`.

### ① Derived judgments

The rule is unchanged: an origin a register or update body names is trusted only for the server-side discovery fetch and validation of that provider, and never as an accepted `Origin` for the request's own origin check, which reads the deployment's configured trusted origins alone.

**Prior M1: closed.** The sign-out-of-IdP capability check (`assertSsoSignOutOfIdpSupported`, `auth-manager.ts`) now builds its own predicate with `trustingBodyNamedOrigins`: the request's predicate, and beside it the origins `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` reads off that request's parsed body.

- Both doors. The check is one function, called from the before-hook on `/sso/register` and on `/sso/update-provider`, and the hand-off is inside it, so it does not depend on the hook's return value (register) or on a hand-off the update block lacks. A register or an update from a configured origin that names the provider's issuer or endpoints and saves the switch on reads the same origins it read on `main`: the candidate set is the same (`issuer` and the five `oidcConfig` endpoints, public-routable hosts only), taken from the parsed body where `main` parsed the raw request, and a plain origin is matched by exact origin, which is how the vendor's predicate matches a non-wildcard entry. The undeclared `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` narrowing of the last head is gone on both.
- Bridge doors. `/admin/sso/register`, `/admin/sso/update-provider` and their siblings re-dispatch through the vendor handler and meet the same hook and the same function; nothing is bridge-specific. A body that names no issuer or endpoint (the Console's Edit Sign-In Options action) yields an empty list, the helper returns the request's predicate itself, and the check reads the configured list, as on `main`.
- Scoped to that one check and that one request. The widened predicate is a closure made per call and passed to `judgeSignOutOfIdpCapability` alone. Nothing writes to `ctx.context.trustedOrigins` or to any shared list; the auth instance's `trustedOrigins` option is still the configured array in every arm; the register endpoint's per-endpoint context change is untouched by these commits; the after-hook that stores the logout endpoint takes the endpoint, not the predicate. I found no path from the body-named origins to the request-origin check, to a callback or redirect validation, or to another request.
- Pins. `sso-discovery-companion-origins.test.ts` gains: a same-origin register with the switch on that saves and keeps the logout endpoint; the same on update, naming the issuer in the update body; a CONTROL that a logout endpoint on a host the body does not name is still refused `400 VALIDATION_FAILED` on `signOutOfIdp` with no row written; a pin that the body-named origin with the switch on is still refused `403 INVALID_ORIGIN` as the request's `Origin` on register and on update, rows unchanged; and a unit pin of the helper (exact origin; other port, other scheme, subdomain, non-http scheme and a non-URL refused; an empty list returns the caller's predicate). By reading, the two door pins are red on `dc13f564` (the configured list alone does not hold the issuer's origin) and the CONTROL is green on both heads. The pins commit precedes the fix commit.
- Declaration. The changeset's Unchanged paragraph is now scoped to a request from a configured origin and names the sign-out read on both doors; the header of `sso-discovery-companion-origins.ts` names the two readers and says the vendor's update endpoint itself reads none; the jsdoc on `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` and the comment in `auth-manager-auth-instance.ts` agree. Each of those statements holds against the code. No second narrowing remains to declare.

**Prior S1: closed.** `content/docs/permissions/sso.mdx` now says what each door does: a registration's discovery and endpoint checks read the named origin, and so does the logout-endpoint check when a registration or an update turns the switch on. That matches the tree; an update without the switch hands its named origins to nothing, and the sentence no longer says otherwise.

**Prior N1: closed.** The changeset subject reads `fix(plugin-auth)!`, as the PR title does.

**New at this head.**

S1 (should-fix) — new. The hand-off that closes prior M1 is wider than the one verdict prior M1 named: the body-named origins reach more of the capability check than its verdict on the logout endpoint, as they did on `main`. Narrow the hand-off to that verdict alone, with a pin per door; if narrowing moves any verdict against `main`, that is the lane's to measure and declare. This is not a regression against `main` and it does not touch the request-origin half, which is why it is not a must-fix; the review seat holds the detail.

S2 (should-fix) — new; continues the PR-body part of prior M1. The PR body was not brought to this head. Its "What changes" still says `/sso/update-provider` "needs no hand-off" and lists no change for the capability check or `trustingBodyNamedOrigins`; its test list omits the five new cases; the maintainer digest promises 18/18 for a file that now holds 23 cases; and every Verification reading names `dc13f5644e`, so no red-before-green or ablation reading is reported for the new pins and no package, typecheck or gate reading for this head. The two declaration lines are right. Editing the body does not move the head.

N1 (nit) — new. The CONTROL for a logout endpoint on a host the body does not name drives the register door only; the update door shares the function and the helper has its own unit pin, so the gap is coverage symmetry, not behaviour. In the same family: the jsdoc on `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` still calls its argument "the vendor endpoint's parsed `/sso/register` body" two paragraphs above the line that says an update body reaches it too.

No must-fix.

### ② Semver level

`patch` on `@objectstack/plugin-auth`, with `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` on both the PR body and the changeset: the level AGENTS.md sets for a breaking change that moves no metadata protocol. The changeset keeps the BREAKING banner, exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`; nothing stored changes shape, so the disposition fits), the from and to of the option (per-request function to the configured list), who moves, and the one-line remedy. With M1 closed the one narrowing it names is the only one in the tree, and its Unchanged paragraph is true as written.

CI at this head: 57 check-runs, all completed; 40 success, 17 skipped. Nothing is running, cancelled or red. This PASS is not rendered over running checks.

### ③ Boundary flags

- The register hand-off still rides the vendor seam the companion origins use (a before-hook's context answer merged per dispatch). The new hand-off does not: it is a plain closure in the plugin's own check, so a vendor change to that merge cannot move it.
- `trustingBodyNamedOrigins` matches by exact origin for `http` and `https` only. It is equivalent to the vendor's predicate for the plain origins `ssoDiscoveryTrustedOrigins` yields; it would not be for a wildcard entry, and that function never yields one.
- Security discipline: this record stays at the rule layer.

### ④ Design judgment

Against the published surface on `main`: the declared narrowing still makes the spec's own refusal real. `trustedOrigins` is documented as the deployment's list, a request body adding to the list its own origin check reads was never a declared capability, and the only client that moves is the one the changeset names.

The last head reasoned about one of the two discovery readers on these doors and narrowed the other without saying so. This head gives the second reader the body-named origins directly, in the function that needs them, on both doors at once, and writes the two readers down in the module header, the jsdoc, the changeset and the docs. For a request from a configured origin the tree now answers as `main` did on every path I could find, and for a request from an unconfigured origin it refuses as declared. The design is sound for the rule it claims. S1 asks for the hand-off to be as narrow inside the check as it is outside it; S2 asks the PR body to describe the head it will land. Neither changes the verdict on the narrowing.
